_meta.description: Expansion set (23 questions) to grow the eval from 17 -> 40. Skewed toward harder patterns the original set did not cover: HAVING, subqueries, correlated/nested aggregates, 4-table joins, window functions, CTEs, self-joins, set operations, and value-repair traps. Merge these into adventureworks_eval.json under the matching category keys.
_meta.status: DRAFT - gold_sql is written from AdventureWorks knowledge and NOT yet validated against the live DB. Run each gold_sql through execute_ms_sql_query first; fix any that error or return 0 rows, then trust it.
_meta.ordered_note: Only items with an explicit "ordered": true enforce row sequence (running totals / YoY). Ranking questions expose the RANK as a COLUMN, so an unordered set comparison already validates them.

b1.prompt: List all departments along with the group they belong to.

b2.prompt: How many products are there in total?
b2.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS ProductCount FROM Production.Product;

b3.prompt: Show the name and list price of the 10 most expensive products.
b3.gold_sql: SELECT TOP 10 Name, ListPrice FROM Production.Product ORDER BY ListPrice DESC;

b4.prompt: List the first name, last name and job title of all employees.
b4.gold_sql: SELECT p.FirstName, p.LastName, e.JobTitle FROM HumanResources.Employee e JOIN Person.Person p ON e.BusinessEntityID = p.BusinessEntityID;

m1.prompt: What is the total sales amount (TotalDue) for each calendar year?
m1.gold_sql: SELECT YEAR(OrderDate) AS OrderYear, SUM(TotalDue) AS TotalSales FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader GROUP BY YEAR(OrderDate) ORDER BY OrderYear;

m2.prompt: How many employees currently work in each department? (use the current assignment only)
m2.gold_sql: SELECT d.Name AS DepartmentName, COUNT(*) AS EmployeeCount FROM HumanResources.Department d JOIN HumanResources.EmployeeDepartmentHistory edh ON d.DepartmentID = edh.DepartmentID WHERE edh.EndDate IS NULL GROUP BY d.Name ORDER BY EmployeeCount DESC;

m3.prompt: List all employees who work in the Human Resources department.
m3.gold_sql: SELECT p.FirstName, p.LastName, e.JobTitle FROM HumanResources.Employee e JOIN Person.Person p ON e.BusinessEntityID = p.BusinessEntityID JOIN HumanResources.EmployeeDepartmentHistory edh ON e.BusinessEntityID = edh.BusinessEntityID JOIN HumanResources.Department d ON edh.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID WHERE d.Name = 'Human Resources' AND edh.EndDate IS NULL;
m3.value_repair_hint: A naive model will likely filter d.Name = 'HR'; the stored value is 'Human Resources'.

m4.prompt: Show all products in the 'Mountain Bikes' subcategory with their list price.
m4.gold_sql: SELECT p.Name, p.ListPrice FROM Production.Product p JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory ps ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID WHERE ps.Name = 'Mountain Bikes';

m5.prompt: Count how many customers are assigned to each sales territory.
m5.gold_sql: SELECT st.Name AS TerritoryName, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Sales.Customer c JOIN Sales.SalesTerritory st ON c.TerritoryID = st.TerritoryID GROUP BY st.Name ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC;

m6.prompt: List the names of all female employees.
m6.gold_sql: SELECT p.FirstName, p.LastName FROM HumanResources.Employee e JOIN Person.Person p ON e.BusinessEntityID = p.BusinessEntityID WHERE e.Gender = 'F';
m6.value_repair_hint: Gender is stored as a single char 'F'/'M', not 'Female'/'Male'.

m7.prompt: How many products are there in each product category?
m7.gold_sql: SELECT pc.Name AS Category, COUNT(*) AS ProductCount FROM Production.Product p JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory ps ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID JOIN Production.ProductCategory pc ON ps.ProductCategoryID = pc.ProductCategoryID GROUP BY pc.Name;

m8.prompt: Show each department name and its employee count where the count > 5.
m8.gold_sql: SELECT d.Name, COUNT(*) AS EmployeeCount FROM HumanResources.Department d JOIN HumanResources.EmployeeDepartmentHistory edh ON d.DepartmentID = edh.DepartmentID WHERE edh.EndDate IS NULL GROUP BY d.Name HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

m9.prompt: How many sales orders were placed in 2013?
m9.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader WHERE YEAR(OrderDate) = 2013;

m10.prompt: Show the name and standard cost of the 10 products with the highest standard cost.
m10.gold_sql: SELECT TOP 10 Name, StandardCost FROM Production.Product ORDER BY StandardCost DESC;

m11.prompt: How many employees were hired in each year?
m11.gold_sql: SELECT YEAR(HireDate) AS HireYear, COUNT(*) AS NumHired FROM HumanResources.Employee GROUP BY YEAR(HireDate) ORDER BY HireYear;

m12.prompt: List the names of all products that are grey in colour.
m12.gold_sql: SELECT Name FROM Production.Product WHERE Color = 'Grey';
m12.value_repair_hint: Stored value is British spelling 'Grey'; a naive model often writes 'Gray'.

m13.prompt: Which sales territories belong to the 'Europe' group?
m13.note: [Group] is a reserved word - tests bracket handling.

h1.prompt: Who are the top 5 customers by total amount spent across all their orders?
h1.gold_sql: SELECT TOP 5 soh.CustomerID, SUM(soh.TotalDue) AS TotalSpent FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader soh GROUP BY soh.CustomerID ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;

h2.prompt: Which product has been sold in the highest total quantity?
h2.gold_sql: SELECT TOP 1 p.Name, SUM(sod.OrderQty) AS TotalQty FROM Sales.SalesOrderDetail sod JOIN Production.Product p ON sod.ProductID = p.ProductID GROUP BY p.Name ORDER BY TotalQty DESC;

h3.prompt: List products that have never been ordered by customers.
h3.gold_sql: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name FROM Production.Product p LEFT JOIN Sales.SalesOrderDetail sod ON p.ProductID = sod.ProductID WHERE sod.ProductID IS NULL;

h4.prompt: For each sales person, show their first/last name and their total sales (TotalDue) for orders they handled.
h4.gold_sql: SELECT p.FirstName, p.LastName, SUM(soh.TotalDue) AS TotalSales FROM Sales.SalesPerson sp JOIN Person.Person p ON sp.BusinessEntityID = p.BusinessEntityID JOIN Sales.SalesOrderHeader soh ON sp.BusinessEntityID = soh.SalesPersonID GROUP BY p.FirstName, p.LastName ORDER BY TotalSales DESC;

h5.prompt: What is the average order total (TotalDue) per month in 2013?
h5.gold_sql: SELECT MONTH(OrderDate) AS OrderMonth, AVG(TotalDue) AS AvgOrderTotal FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader WHERE YEAR(OrderDate) = 2013 GROUP BY MONTH(OrderDate) ORDER BY OrderMonth;

h6.prompt: List the top 3 product subcategories by total revenue (LineTotal).
h6.gold_sql: SELECT TOP 3 ps.Name AS Subcategory, SUM(sod.LineTotal) AS Revenue FROM Sales.SalesOrderDetail sod JOIN Production.Product p ON sod.ProductID = p.ProductID JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory ps ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID GROUP BY ps.Name ORDER BY Revenue DESC;

h7.prompt: Show each customer and their count where order count > 5 ?
h7.gold_sql: SELECT soh.CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader soh GROUP BY soh.CustomerID HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY OrderCount DESC;

h8.prompt: List product names whose list price is above the average list price of all products.
h8.gold_sql: SELECT Name, ListPrice FROM Production.Product WHERE ListPrice > (SELECT AVG(ListPrice) FROM Production.Product);

h9.prompt: What is the total sales revenue (LineTotal) for each product category?
h9.gold_sql: SELECT pc.Name AS Category, SUM(sod.LineTotal) AS Revenue FROM Sales.SalesOrderDetail sod JOIN Production.Product p ON sod.ProductID = p.ProductID JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory ps ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID JOIN Production.ProductCategory pc ON ps.ProductCategoryID = pc.ProductCategoryID GROUP BY pc.Name ORDER BY Revenue DESC;

h10.prompt: List the first and last name of every sales person along with their sales quota.
h10.gold_sql: SELECT p.FirstName, p.LastName, sp.SalesQuota FROM Sales.SalesPerson sp JOIN Person.Person p ON sp.BusinessEntityID = p.BusinessEntityID;

h11.prompt: Which products have been manufactured (appear in work orders) but never sold?
h11.gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.ProductID, p.Name FROM Production.Product p JOIN Production.WorkOrder wo ON p.ProductID = wo.ProductID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Sales.SalesOrderDetail sod WHERE sod.ProductID = p.ProductID);

h12.prompt: Show the territory name and its average order total.
h12.gold_sql: SELECT st.Name AS Territory, AVG(soh.TotalDue) AS AvgOrderTotal FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader soh JOIN Sales.SalesTerritory st ON soh.TerritoryID = st.TerritoryID GROUP BY st.Name ORDER BY AvgOrderTotal DESC;

h13.prompt: Which customers spent more than the average total spend across all customers?
h13.gold_sql: SELECT CustomerID, SUM(TotalDue) AS TotalSpent FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING SUM(TotalDue) > (SELECT AVG(cust_total) FROM (SELECT SUM(TotalDue) AS cust_total FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader GROUP BY CustomerID) t);

h14.prompt: Show the product name and its distinct-customer count.
h14.gold_sql: SELECT p.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT soh.CustomerID) AS DistinctCustomers FROM Production.Product p JOIN Sales.SalesOrderDetail sod ON p.ProductID = sod.ProductID JOIN Sales.SalesOrderHeader soh ON sod.SalesOrderID = soh.SalesOrderID GROUP BY p.Name ORDER BY DistinctCustomers DESC;

e1.prompt: Rank the products within each subcategory by list price (highest first), showing subcategory, product name, list price and the rank
e1.gold_sql: SELECT ps.Name AS Subcategory, p.Name AS Product, p.ListPrice, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ps.ProductSubcategoryID ORDER BY p.ListPrice DESC) AS PriceRank FROM Production.Product p JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory ps ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID;

e2.prompt: For each sales person, show their total sales (TotalDue) and their rank among all sales persons by total sales.
e2.gold_sql: SELECT sp.BusinessEntityID, SUM(soh.TotalDue) AS TotalSales, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(soh.TotalDue) DESC) AS SalesRank FROM Sales.SalesPerson sp JOIN Sales.SalesOrderHeader soh ON sp.BusinessEntityID = soh.SalesPersonID GROUP BY sp.BusinessEntityID;

e3.prompt: Show the 3 most expensive products in each product category, considering all products.
e3.gold_sql: SELECT Category, Product, ListPrice FROM (SELECT pc.Name AS Category, p.Name AS Product, p.ListPrice, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pc.ProductCategoryID ORDER BY p.ListPrice DESC) AS rn FROM Production.Product p JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory ps ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID JOIN Production.ProductCategory pc ON ps.ProductCategoryID = pc.ProductCategoryID) t WHERE rn <= 3;

e4.prompt: Show pairs of products with their name that share the same list price (list each pair once, ignore products with price 0).
e4.gold_sql: SELECT p1.Name AS ProductA, p2.Name AS ProductB, p1.ListPrice FROM Production.Product p1 JOIN Production.Product p2 ON p1.ListPrice = p2.ListPrice AND p1.ProductID < p2.ProductID WHERE p1.ListPrice > 0;

e5.prompt: Show total sales per year and the year-over-year change in total sales.
e5.gold_sql: WITH yearly AS (SELECT YEAR(OrderDate) AS yr, SUM(TotalDue) AS total FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader GROUP BY YEAR(OrderDate)) SELECT yr, total, total - LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY yr) AS YoYChange FROM yearly ORDER BY yr;

e6.prompt: Show the name of products that have been sold but are not part of any promotional special offer (excluding the default 'No Discount' offer).
e6.gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.ProductID, p.Name FROM Production.Product p JOIN Sales.SalesOrderDetail sod ON p.ProductID = sod.ProductID WHERE p.ProductID NOT IN (SELECT ProductID FROM Sales.SpecialOfferProduct WHERE SpecialOfferID <> 1);

e7.prompt: Show all sales territory with thier name and the percentage of total company sales revenue comes from them.
e7.gold_sql: SELECT st.Name AS Territory, SUM(soh.TotalDue) AS Revenue, 100.0 * SUM(soh.TotalDue) / SUM(SUM(soh.TotalDue)) OVER () AS PctOfTotal FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader soh JOIN Sales.SalesTerritory st ON soh.TerritoryID = st.TerritoryID GROUP BY st.Name ORDER BY Revenue DESC;

e8.prompt: For each month of 2013, show the monthly sales total and the running cumulative sales total through the year.
e8.gold_sql: SELECT MONTH(OrderDate) AS OrderMonth, SUM(TotalDue) AS MonthlyTotal, SUM(SUM(TotalDue)) OVER (ORDER BY MONTH(OrderDate)) AS RunningTotal FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader WHERE YEAR(OrderDate) = 2013 GROUP BY MONTH(OrderDate) ORDER BY OrderMonth;
